author: Jessica Thompson
title: DHS Threatens Action Against States Defying ICE - NewsBreak
text:
By Jessica Thompson ,
18 minutes ago The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has intensified pressure on certain Democrat-led states, demanding that they inform U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) about the release of inmates from state custody. ICE Acting Director Todd Lyons has warned of legal repercussions for officials in California, New York, and Illinois if they fail to comply, prompting a sharp response from Illinois Attorney General Kwame Raoul, who highlighted the risks of liability due to errors in ICE detainer requests.
In a letter, Lyons stated, “ICE will engage with the U.S. Department of Justice and other federal partners to pursue all appropriate measures against you,” signaling potential legal action against non-compliant states.
Raoul countered, emphasizing the risks of faulty detainer information, saying, “Responding to an ICE detainer based on erroneous information could subject Illinois law enforcement agencies to liability for ICE’s mistakes.” He added, “And unfortunately, the number of erroneous detentions by ICE continues to grow at an alarming pace.”
DHS emphasized that it had specifically requested the attorneys general of California, New York, and Illinois to notify ICE about the release of inmates. DHS Assistant Secretary Tricia McLaughlin argued that sanctuary policies in these states obstruct federal immigration enforcement efforts, potentially allowing dangerous individuals to be released into communities.
DHS clarified its position, stating, “ICE detainers ask for something very simple: To notify ICE when criminal illegal aliens are released from jail or prison, to ensure that they go into ICE custody before they are released back onto our streets.”
McLaughlin further criticized state policies, asserting, “These dangerous sanctuary policies, often combined with cashless bail for serious crimes, allow criminal illegal aliens to be released back into American communities, threatening the American people’s lives and wellbeing.”
Civil rights advocates have raised concerns that complying with ICE detainers, particularly when based on inaccurate records, could violate constitutional protections and lead to wrongful detentions. DHS has indicated it may refer the issue to the Department of Justice for further action if the states continue to resist cooperation.
Jessica Thompson covers U.S. politics & news for content partner Modern Newsstand LLC.
